system.name: Melange legislative activity and effectiveness data (incl. Draft Systems R pipeline)
system.description: Upstream legislative inputs: the congress.gov activity scrape with Congress decay, Ballotpedia committee, caucus and party-leadership scores, the signal-prioritized press collector cap, the release category taxonomy, synthetic billstatus rows, the sentinel bill ledger with strongest-role dedup, and the five-stage legislative-effectiveness shadow (Volden-Wiseman style) with its CEL criterion.

components.name: congress.gov legislative activity score with Congress decay
components.computes: Per member x 17 sections x 3 roles: bill counts, average cosponsors and success rate, with counts decayed by 0.8^age per Congress (138 columns).
components.method: Role swap on search URLs. Success comes from status text with a fallback classifier. The sentinel ledger also applies 0.8^(119-c) and keeps the strongest role per bill.
assumptions: Recent Congresses matter more by a constant factor
empirical_questions: Does a 0.8 per-Congress decay maximize prediction of current-Congress CU activity from past activity?
components.heading: congress.gov legislative activity score with Congress decay

components.name: Ballotpedia committee, caucus and party-leadership scores
components.computes: Committee leadership (Chair 1.0 ... Member 0.2), caucus leadership, party leadership (Speaker 1.0 ... Minority Whip 0.2) and a weighted electoral average (2018 x2).
components.method: Bioguide-keyed (this fixed a five-Johnsons bug). Sub Layer AW:BA is normalized by x/max.
assumptions: Leadership positions indicate CU leverage (hand-set constants)
empirical_questions: Does party leadership rank predict effectiveness on CU bills?
components.heading: Ballotpedia committee, caucus and party-leadership scores

components.name: Signal-prioritized press collection cap
components.computes: Per-member URL cap (default 1000) prioritized by CU-term titles.
components.method: Coverage 86.6% before fixes. P(CU-relevant | CU-term title) = 0.825 vs 0.0089 for generic titles. Coverage: D 92.5% vs R 87%; Senate 83% vs House 96%.
assumptions: CU-term titles proxy CU relevance; missing pages carry about 10% CU signal
empirical_questions: Does differential coverage by party or chamber bias the press pillar?
components.heading: Signal-prioritized press collection cap

components.name: Release category taxonomy and billstatus synthetic rows
components.computes: 19 Layer-2 categories under 7 groups via regex, net and count per member; synthetic 'X (co)sponsored' rows from BILLSTATUS XML.
components.method: Billstatus rows were removed from Stage 5 on 2026-06-30; 110 members then had no real releases.
assumptions: Regex terms identify a release's topic
Cosponsorship is a press-layer signal (later rejected)
empirical_questions: What is the precision of regex topic tagging against human coding?
components.heading: Release category taxonomy and billstatus synthetic rows

components.name: Five-stage legislative effectiveness shadow and CEL criterion
components.computes: Role-weighted, timing-decayed credit per stage (BILL, AIC, ABC, PASS, LAW), normalized N/5 per chamber-term, decayed 0.8 per Congress. Results-only and 70/30 advocacy composite percentiles. Ceremonial-share criterion against CEL LES.
components.method: Role weights 3/2/1; cosponsor timing 2^(-delay/180); impact weights 1/5/10. A shadow candidate, not activated.
assumptions: More conscientious members sponsor fewer ceremonial bills (RKH)
empirical_questions: Does the shadow score converge with published CEL LES for the same members and Congresses?
Does cosponsor timing (early joiners) predict bill advancement?
components.heading: Five-stage legislative effectiveness shadow and CEL criterion

positions.paul_position: Paul wants a pipeline from public records. He highlighted Ardekani's point that legislation is machine-readable, with the margin note 'Same for the US?'.
Leadership insulates members from the broader ecosystem (Gaynor), and senior leaders hold the broadest community memberships (Kim & Kunisky).
Paul highlighted LES as the effectiveness criterion and Sotoudeh's contrast with it.

evidence.title: Mapping Political Communities: A Statistical Analysis of Lobbying Networks in Legislative Politics
evidence.claim: Legislators with the most legislation-community memberships are often senior politicians or party leaders, and high-entropy legislators (entropy >= 2, roughly 4+ communities) sit on power committees. The paper measures breadth of lobbying interaction, not leverage.
evidence.system_side: Hand-set constants: committee leadership Chair 1.0, Ranking 0.8, Vice Chair 0.6, Vice Ranking 0.4, Member 0.2; party leadership Speaker 1, President pro tempore 1, Majority Leader 0.8, Minority Leader 0.6, Majority Whip 0.4, Minority Whip 0.2.
evidence.transfer: Consistent with scoring leadership as general reach rather than CU-specific leverage; the 'diluted industry share' reading is the analyst's inference. Says nothing about effectiveness on CU bills. One Congress, descriptive.

evidence.title: Identifying hidden coalitions in the US House of Representatives by optimally partitioning signed networks based on generalized balance
evidence.claim: Effectiveness is the CEL LES: fifteen indicators, normalized to mean 1 per session. The paper compares coalition-mean LES with 95% CI bands across party, k=2 and k=3 partitions. The third coalition is the most effective in most sessions and is anchored by a few members (e.g. Christopher Smith, mean effectiveness 8.44, 106th-108th).
evidence.system_side: lep_criterion.py loads CEL House and Senate data (93rd-118th) from fec/lep/*.dta (CELHouse93to118Reduced.dta, CELSenate93to118Reduced.dta), including lesclassic and dwnom1, for a pre-registered convergence look against the blended score.
evidence.transfer: The LES half of the comparison is already local. Reproducing it also needs a House-only, per-Congress signed co-sponsorship backbone and a k=3 partition, and neither is built. The result would be descriptive, with no controls for majority or chair status, which drive LES. It stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it (DE-062). Any pooled comparison across sessions must be stratified by majority party or labelled UNSTRATIFIED.

evidence.title: Measuring Elite Personality Using Speech
evidence.claim: Conscientiousness lowers the ceremonial share of sponsored bills: -0.52 (M1), -0.39 (M3), -0.53 (M4), -0.58 (M5, Congress FE), all p<0.01. Majority x C is +0.27 (M4) and +0.29 (M5), so the C effect is smallest in the majority. N = 3,648 member-Congresses in M3 to M5, 104th to 112th Congresses; binomial regression with implicit weighting by bills proposed (fn 37).
evidence.system_side: lep_criterion.py computes Spearman rho between pooled ceremonial share (115th to 118th Congresses, at least 8 bills) and diligence_z, lexical C v1 and behaviour-calibrated C v2. Stored data/members/lep_criterion.json: rho 0.0026, 0.0176 and 0.0003, n = 440, all null. There is no majority split. The script's own comment (lines 127-128) says the test is attenuated.
evidence.transfer: The paper's effect is minority-concentrated, so a pooled rank correlation is an UNSTRATIFIED test of a conditional claim. Modern Congresses carry few ceremonial bills, which attenuates the test. A stratified, bill-weighted re-run is new analysis and stays UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces it.

evidence.title: A Network-Based Measure of Cosponsorship Influence on Bill Passing in the United States House of Representatives
evidence.claim: Shorter decay gives slightly more separation within the tested range: relative differences 0.248, 0.223 and 0.203 at 6, 12 and 24-month half-lives (SE 0.0139, 0.0119, 0.0107). The paper lists a comparison with LES as future work and does not run it.
evidence.system_side: Shadow uses Volden-Wiseman-style stages with role weights 3/2/1, a 180-day cosponsor timing half-life and congress decay 0.8 (confirmed in code). The 0.8 per Congress equals a half-life of about 3.1 Congresses, far longer than the 24-month maximum the paper tested.
evidence.transfer: The paper proposes an LES comparison; it does not propose a sub-Congress decay check, and it already tested 6 and 12-month half-lives. Its outcome (separating passed from failed bills) differs from the shadow's goal (convergence with LES), so it cannot set the decay value. Its evidence covers only 6-24 months.

evidence.title: Inferring social networks from unstructured text data: A proof of concept detection of hidden communities of interest
evidence.claim: k was chosen by combining Cv coherence (scanned over k = 5 to 100, with no coherence gain above 35) and manual reading of top words; any topic model is acceptable if assignments are continuous probabilities rather than crisp.
evidence.system_side: The HCoI profile input is a regex categorisation into 20 CU press categories, not 19: 20 entries in the CATEGORIES block of cu_press_release_scraper.R and 20 categories in the stored press_hcoi.json. Each item's labels are crisp and split evenly (press_hcoi.py lines 25-27, 45). No precision check against human coding and no coherence or overlap check on the categories was found.
evidence.transfer: The continuous-assignment requirement is met only loosely: member profiles are continuous after averaging, item tags are crisp. A coherence-selected LDA on the same corpus or a precision sample of the regex tags would show whether communities reflect the taxonomy or the text. Any result stays a diagnostic until reproduced.

evidence.title: Inferring social networks from unstructured text data: A proof of concept detection of hidden communities of interest
evidence.claim: The quality of an HCoI network depends on the representativeness of the corpus, which is crucial for conclusions. The authors also flag the venues and languages they left out.
evidence.system_side: cu_text_collector.R caps each member at 1000 URLs by default (CU_TC_CAP, line 128), taking CU-candidate titled pages first and a sample of the rest. The coverage percentages in the analyst output (D 92.5 vs R 87; Senate 83 vs House 96) were not located in the code and were not verified.
evidence.transfer: The caution applies. Before reading HCoI membership substantively, check party and chamber gaps in who is profiled (155 members profiled in the current artifact). Any figure should name its window and denominator.

evidence.title: The (Financial) Ties That Bind: Social Networks of Intraparty Caucuses
evidence.claim: Leadership predicts higher outward LPAC degree. Paul Ryan gave to 195 members and Joe Crowley to 80. Republican leaders give to 86% of members but about 30% of Freedom Caucus members (Table 4 Freedom -0.816***). Leader models use the full-party networks; the 238 R and 168 D connected-node counts are in the Table 2-3 notes, and Tables 4-5 give no N.
evidence.system_side: party_caucus_score: Speaker and President pro tempore 1.0, Majority Leader 0.8, Minority Leader 0.6, Majority Whip 0.4, Minority Whip 0.2. cu_caucus_leadership_score: Chair 1.0 and Co-Chair/Vice Chair 0.8 across 13 CU-relevant caucuses. Rank-and-file membership scores 0 and is not counted. No ideological intraparty caucus is on the list.
evidence.transfer: Paper treats ideological intraparty caucus membership as a structural variable for within-party money flows. System records only policy-caucus leadership. Adding faction membership needs a dated 119th Congress roster; the paper's Yellow Book membership is self-reported (fn.6). Membership would describe position in party, not CU leverage.

evidence.title: Cue-Taking in Congress: Interest Group Signals from Dear Colleague Letters
evidence.claim: Stage-specific coefficients (Tables 3-4): endorser social power predicts cosponsors (0.055) but not reporting (0.020) or passage (-0.035). Endorser count predicts passage (0.013) but not reporting (0.004, ns). Cosponsor count predicts reporting (0.002, p<.01) and passage (0.004, p<.001).
evidence.system_side: legislative_effectiveness.py lines 17-28 confirmed: stages BILL, AIC, ABC, PASS, LAW; role weights; cosponsor_half_life_days 180; policy_status shadow_candidate, consistent with not activated.
evidence.transfer: The paper gives stage-specific coefficients on one sample of letter bills (N = 6,597) and does not argue for stage-based modelling; the stage pattern is an empirical observation only. It does not test cosponsor timing decay and gives no support for the 180-day half-life. Pooled, UNSTRATIFIED.

evidence.title: Is Bigger Always Better? Potential Biases of Big Data Derived from Social Network Sites
evidence.claim: A sampling frame tied to the outcome can bias findings (Schwartz et al. 2013 opt-in app users, p. 65). Studies should state the frame scope and keep sampling separate from the outcome.
evidence.system_side: cu_text_collector.R lines 112-140: every CU-candidate-titled page is fetched; generic pages are capped at CAP = 1000 per member, newest first (confirmed). Registry figures (P(CU-relevant given CU title) 0.825 vs 0.0089; coverage D 92.5 vs R 87, Senate 83 vs House 96) match the component registry text; not re-measured from the corpus.
evidence.transfer: Hargittai's argument applies only if coverage gaps correlate with CU stance or volume. The cap drops only generic pages (about 0.9 percent CU-relevant per the registry). The cap is not party- or chamber-specific, so 'favours House and Democratic offices' does not follow from the code; it rests on unmeasured coverage rates. The collector comment assumes the skipped bulk is missing at random, which is the untested premise.

evidence.title: How to train your stochastic parrot: large language models for political texts
evidence.claim: LLM topic labels can be checked with an optimal-label task. In 400 speeches a blinded coder picked the GPT-3 label over three random intruders 80 percent of the time, against 25 percent chance. Keyword presence overcounts: 5332 speeches contain honor, but only 145 are labelled as praising it.
evidence.system_side: Release and post categories come from regex keyword maps (CATKW = MR.RAW_PATTERNS at build_media_blend.py:50). No human-label check of those regex tags was found in the files read. Downstream use (media blend, press category weights) was not traced.
evidence.transfer: The paper labels are open-ended virtue labels for 2013-2014 House speeches; Melange uses fixed CU policy categories on releases and posts. The intruder protocol transfers as a measurement check on existing regex tags. Adopting LLM-assigned categories would be a separate decision. The R scraper CATEGORIES regex was not opened.

evidence.title: Legislative Effectiveness in the American States
evidence.claim: SLES is a weighted average of 15 indicators: five stage shares (introduced, AIC, ABC, passed chamber, law) at three significance weights (1, 5, 10), normalized by N/5 so each chamber-term averages 1 (Eq. 1). Window 1987-2018, 97 chambers, 80,344 legislator-term scores. Hand audit: 46,693 of 49,037 sampled bills (95.2%) correctly coded, over 99% after revision. North Carolina 2005-2012: SLES explains about half the variation in NCCPPR rankings and beats hit-rate metrics.
evidence.system_side: fec/engine/legislative_effectiveness.py: STAGES at line 17; role weights sponsor 3, original 2, cosponsor 1 at lines 18-19; impact weights limited to 1, 5, 10 at line 232; letters forced to weight 5 at line 228; congress_decay 0.8 at lines 29 and 482; normalization N/5 per chamber and Congress at line 500; cosponsor timing multiplier 2 to the power of minus delay over 180 at line 132; status shadow_candidate at line 31. effectiveness_integration.py line 111 holds the 0.7 advocacy and 0.3 results composite. The CU-mention significance source was not found in this file; the weight arrives from an upstream impact record (line 225).
evidence.transfer: The stage, weight and normalization structure transfers to the federal shadow as a structural adaptation. The paper's validation covers sponsor-based state SLES with newspaper-coded significance; it does not validate cosponsor role credit, the 180-day timing decay, letters at weight 5, or the 70/30 composite. Those stay UNVERIFIED until checked against CEL LES for the same members and Congresses.

evidence.title: Detecting coalitions by optimally partitioning signed networks of political collaboration
evidence.claim: House bill passage rate fell 0.11 pp per session (beta -0.528, p<0.05); Senate fell 0.35 pp per session (beta -0.852, p<0.01). What mediates passage differs by chamber.
evidence.system_side: Shadow normalizes stage credit as population/5 within each originating chamber and Congress, then applies a Congress decay (policy default 0.8) to chamber-term results.
evidence.transfer: The paper's passage rate is a chamber-session share of bills. It does not discuss normalization, stage weights or decay, so it supports within-chamber normalization only by analogy. Its measure is chamber-level, covers 1979-2016, and is association rather than cause.

evidence.title: CampaignView, a database of policy platforms and biographical narratives for congressional candidates
evidence.claim: Each platform point is hand-coded by trained annotators to one of 14 Major Policy Topic codes using a codebook. A 20% relabel (8,584 points, by 2022 coders) gave 80% agreement, Cohen kappa 0.84 and weighted kappa 0.74, with most disagreement on Unknown/Other.
evidence.system_side: cu_press_release_scraper.R defines 19 Layer-2 categories by regex term lists plus bill-based tags. detect_categories tags a release with EVERY category it touches, so the tagger is multi-label, not single-topic. A human-label kappa exists for stance (run_stage5.R line 133: regex 0.17, DEBATE 0.34). No topic-level reliability benchmark was found.
evidence.transfer: Transfers as a validation design (double-code a random sample, report kappa), not as labels: genre and topic scheme differ from CU categories. The paper's single-topic rule under-codes multi-topic text, but the regex tagger does not share that rule.

evidence.title: Bulk Ingestion of Congressional Actions and Materials Dataset (BICAM)
evidence.claim: Bulk bills, amendments, committees and members from the official APIs with rolling updates. Retrieving the full set directly needs over 100 endpoints, a 5,000 requests per hour cap, and at least 10 requests per bill.
evidence.system_side: sync_sentinel_bill_ledger.py decay_weight gives 1.0 for Congress 119, 0.8 for 118 and 0.64 for 117, described in the code as the frozen legacy archive schedule. The code read does not show that this weight feeds the activity score. The congress.gov search-URL scraping in R was not inspected.
evidence.transfer: Sourcing cross-check only. Reconciling scraped counts against BICAM sponsor and cosponsor tables would need a run first. Remains UNVERIFIED.

evidence.title: Politics of Feelings: Emotional Expression and Legislative Effectiveness in the U.S. Congress
evidence.claim: On member-Congress LES (n = 13,671; Tables 7-9, all models with session and topic fixed effects): anger -0.037 (95% CI -0.046 to -0.029, p < 0.001) is the only significant negative emotion term; enthusiasm +0.016 (CI 0.007 to 0.025) and pride +0.011 (CI 0.003 to 0.019, p < 0.01) are positive; fear, disgust, sadness, joy and hope are not significant. Marginal R2 is 0.113 to 0.118 in Tables 7-8 and 0.118 to 0.119 in Table 9. The paper reports no controls-only model, so an incremental R2 for emotion terms is not stated.
evidence.system_side: lep_criterion.py loads CEL House and Senate LES 93rd-118th and scores it against the blended score (bar B: rho >= +0.30 convergent). Its docstring says LES rewards majority and chair status. The claim that the five-stage shadow is not activated was not checked (outside the lines read).
evidence.transfer: Transfers as context only: speech tone is a small associational correlate of LES once structural controls are in, so a shadow-vs-LES gap should not be read as a rhetoric effect. No identification, so not usable as a predictor. Quote coefficients as UNSTRATIFIED with window 93rd-118th Congresses and n = 13,671 member-Congresses; the paper pools over majority-flip fault lines.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of Connected Legislators
evidence.claim: Network spillovers are positive at every stage. Corrected phi is 0.5634 (SE 0.0539) for BILL only, 0.8387 (SE 0.0465) for BILL plus AIC and 0.8643 (SE 0.0767) for ABC plus PASS plus LAW, with the selection term significant in each (BILL xi = -0.1601, SE 0.0687). House, 109th-113th.
evidence.system_side: legislative_effectiveness.py scores the five stages with standard role weights 3/2/1 and has no peer or network spillover term. Its cosponsor weight carries a 180-day half-life. lep_criterion.py loads CEL LES (lesclassic) and scores convergence against the blended score only.
evidence.transfer: A spillover term needs a network that is exogenous or corrected relative to the stage outcomes. Paul's cosponsor edges are partly built from the same bills the shadow credits, which is a circularity risk. Any test stays UNVERIFIED until reproduced by a second path.

evidence.title: The Bipartisan Path to Effective Lawmaking
evidence.claim: Stage models use a member's count of bills reaching each stage as the DV, with legislator FE and one-tailed tests. House: committee action (A8.2) 0.894 SE 0.204; beyond committee (A8.3) 0.853; passing chamber (A8.4) 0.800; law (A8.5) 0.485 SE 0.088; all p<0.001. Senate: committee action (A9.2) 1.767, not significant; law (A9.5) 0.589, p<0.05.
evidence.system_side: legislative_effectiveness.py defines STAGES BILL AIC ABC PASS LAW (line 17), role weights sponsor 3, original 2, cosponsor 1 (lines 18-19), a cosponsor timing multiplier of 2 to the power of minus delay over 180 (line 132), and compute_effectiveness (line 152). There is no cross-party term. I found no code that compares the shadow score with the Volden-Wiseman LES; verify_effectiveness_shadow.py checks internal consistency only.
evidence.transfer: The paper DVs are counts of a member's own bills at each stage, not stage rates and not LES. A shadow-vs-LES check would need a per-Congress attracted share (not built) and a comparable LES series. It stays a diagnostic. Quote the coefficients as count-DV associations, House and Senate separately.

evidence.title: The Effects of Congressional Staff Networks in the U.S. House of Representatives
evidence.claim: Members sharing senior staff have modestly correlated LES net of covariates (pooled rho 0.043). Committee chair direct effect is 1.853 (90% CI 1.376 to 2.352); indirect effect via ties is 0.442 (90% CI 0.131 to 0.826).
evidence.system_side: The five-stage shadow score (BILL, AIC, ABC, PASS, LAW) in the cited engine file is a versioned illustrative candidate policy that requires calibration. The claim that it is validated against CEL LES for ceremonial share only is not in the cited engine file; the ceremonial-share and CEL work sits in fec/members/lep_criterion.py. I found no network-similarity check in the cited files.
evidence.transfer: Optional second criterion: shadow scores should show a similar small lag on senior-title ties if they track LES. This is UNVERIFIED, needs office_moves restricted to senior titles, and is not evidence that the shadow score is valid.
